title: ID Churn Sentinel consumer page manifest v1
description: A consumer-authored list of THEIR OWN pages, each naming the government source URLs it cites and the date a person last reviewed it. Read by `sentinel stale`. This file never leaves the consumer's machine and is never sent anywhere: there is no account, no subscriber list, and no network call in the command that reads it.

site.description: A name for the site or organization, echoed back in the report. Optional and purely for the reader.

id.description: Your identifier for the page. Unique within the manifest; echoed in every row.

url.description: Where your page lives. Optional; never fetched.

last_reviewed.description: The date a person last reviewed this page. Staleness is measured from here against each change's `observed_at` — when the government page was observed to change — NOT against the date a reviewer confirmed it. A source that changed before your review date is not stale for you, even if it was confirmed afterwards.

cites.description: The government source URLs this page cites. Matched against the registry exactly, after a conservative normalization (scheme and host lowercased, default port dropped, fragment dropped). Trailing slashes and query strings are NOT stripped: a citation differing only by a slash is reported as `host_only`, which is true, rather than as `matched`, which would be a guess.
